titulo.en: Telling a plot in the present

texto.en: A synopsis, la sinopsis, is a short summary of a novel, film or series. In Spanish it is told in the present tense, even though the work was written long ago: Un joven viaja a Comala para buscar a su padre. You already know this use from the historical present, which makes a story feel as if it were happening now. English synopses work the same way, but when you talk about a book you read last year it is easy to slip into the past, as in Juan viajó…. In a summary, stay in the present from the first sentence to the last.

titulo.en: What happened before, and your opinion

texto.en: Events that happened before the plot begins can go in the past, or in a short phrase with tras + infinitive or después de + haber + participle: Tras morir su madre, Juan viaja a Comala, which means After his mother dies, Juan travels to Comala. Después de haber perdido su casa, la familia viaja a la capital. Your comments on the work are also in the present: El autor logra crear una atmósfera misteriosa. Useful verbs are narrar, contar, retratar, girar en torno a and descubrir. Narrar, contar and retratar take their object directly, as in La novela retrata la soledad, and with a person you need the personal a: busca a su padre.

contexto.en: Thursday, June 3, 2032, in a café in La Floresta. It is the first meeting of the reading club of Sofía, Mateo and Emma. All three use tú with each other. Sofía asks Emma to summarize “Pedro Páramo,” the novel they are reading, as a synopsis.

dialogo.texto: Buenas tardes, chicos. Bienvenidos a la primera sesión del club de lectura. Hoy hablamos de «Pedro Páramo», y quiero empezar con algo práctico: una sinopsis. Emma, ¿puedes contar la trama en pocas palabras?

traduccion.en: Good afternoon, guys. Welcome to the first session of the reading club. Today we talk about “Pedro Páramo,” and I want to start with something practical: a synopsis. Emma, can you tell the plot in a few words?

dialogo.texto: Claro, Sofía. Tras morir su madre, un joven llamado Juan Preciado viaja a Comala para buscar a su padre, Pedro Páramo. Su madre se lo pidió antes de morir.

traduccion.en: Sure, Sofía. After his mother dies, a young man named Juan Preciado travels to Comala to look for his father, Pedro Páramo. His mother asked him to do it before she died.

dialogo.texto: Muy bien. Mateo, fíjate: Emma usa el presente para la trama y el pasado para lo que pasó antes del viaje. Así se escribe una sinopsis. Y ahora dime, Emma, ¿qué descubre Juan cuando llega al pueblo?

traduccion.en: Very good. Mateo, notice: Emma uses the present for the plot and the past for what happened before the trip. That is how a synopsis is written. And now tell me, Emma, what does Juan discover when he arrives in the town?

dialogo.texto: Descubre que el pueblo está lleno de voces de muertos. Todos murieron hace años, pero sus voces siguen ahí, y le cuentan la historia de su padre, un hombre poderoso y cruel. La novela retrata cómo ese hombre deja morir a su pueblo.

traduccion.en: He discovers that the town is full of the voices of the dead. They all died years ago, but their voices are still there, and they tell him the story of his father, a powerful and cruel man. The novel portrays how that man lets his town die.

dialogo.texto: Perfecto. Mateo, tú tienes algo que añadir sobre el giro argumental, ¿verdad?

traduccion.en: Perfect. Mateo, you have something to add about the plot twist, right?

dialogo.texto: Sí. A la mitad del libro, el propio Juan muere, y la historia sigue con las voces del pueblo. Ese giro argumental cambia todo. En el desenlace, Pedro Páramo muere y con él termina Comala.

traduccion.en: Yes. Halfway through the book, Juan himself dies, and the story goes on with the voices of the town. That plot twist changes everything. In the ending, Pedro Páramo dies and Comala ends with him.

dialogo.texto: Mateo, tú eres de Guadalajara. ¿Qué dices sobre el autor?

traduccion.en: Mateo, you are from Guadalajara. What do you say about the author?

dialogo.texto: Juan Rulfo es de Jalisco, como yo. El autor logra crear una atmósfera misteriosa con muy pocas palabras. La ambientación es tan fuerte que casi puedes sentir el calor y el polvo de Comala.

traduccion.en: Juan Rulfo is from Jalisco, like me. The author manages to create a mysterious atmosphere with very few words. The setting is so strong that you can almost feel the heat and the dust of Comala.

dialogo.texto: Esa es otra regla: el comentario sobre la obra también va en presente. Por ejemplo: la novela gira en torno a la búsqueda de un padre y a la soledad de un lugar olvidado.

traduccion.en: That is another rule: the comment on the work also goes in the present. For example: the novel revolves around the search for a father and the loneliness of a forgotten place.

dialogo.texto: Me gusta contar así, porque la historia parece nueva cada vez. ¿Y la tarea para la próxima sesión?

traduccion.en: I like to tell it this way, because the story seems new every time. And what is the homework for the next session?

dialogo.texto: Cada uno escribe una sinopsis de tres oraciones, en presente, de una novela o una película latinoamericana que conozca. Nos vemos el jueves 10 de junio, aquí mismo.

traduccion.en: Each of you writes a three-sentence synopsis, in the present, of a Latin American novel or film you know. See you on Thursday, June 10, right here.

dialogo.texto: Yo voy a hablar de una película mexicana. Voy a empezar esta noche, porque la historia me gusta mucho.

traduccion.en: I am going to talk about a Mexican film. I am going to start tonight, because I like the story a lot.

dialogo.texto: Yo prefiero una novela. Tengo muchas ganas de leer tu sinopsis, Mateo. Y también quiero saber cómo cuentas el desenlace.

traduccion.en: I prefer a novel. I am looking forward to reading your synopsis, Mateo. And I also want to know how you tell the ending.

dialogo.texto: Excelente. Entonces hasta el jueves. Gracias por venir, chicos, y recuerden: la sinopsis siempre va en presente.

traduccion.en: Excellent. Then until Thursday. Thank you for coming, guys, and remember: the synopsis always goes in the present.

explicacion.en: Without the question marks the thought looks like an ordinary sentence. In free indirect style the ¿…? and ¡…! are the main clue that this is a character's voice.

titulo.en: Three ways to report a thought

texto.en: A story can report what a character says or thinks in three ways. Direct style gives the exact words: —¿Dónde está mi padre? —preguntó Juan. Indirect style uses a speech verb and que: Juan preguntó que dónde estaba su padre. Free indirect style, el estilo indirecto libre, has neither a speech verb nor que: the narrator slips into the character's mind and the thought just appears: Juan miró el pueblo. ¿Dónde estaba su padre? You read a question in the third person and in the past, with no dash and no quotation marks. English authors do the same, so the idea is not new to you; what changes is how Spanish marks it.

titulo.en: How to recognize it

texto.en: Free indirect style keeps the narrator's person and tenses, so the changes are the ones you know from indirect speech: the present becomes the imperfect, from está to estaba, the present perfect becomes the pluperfect, from he podido to había podido, mi becomes su and aquí becomes allí. But it keeps the character's own questions and exclamations: ¿Cómo había podido olvidarlo? ¡Qué tarde se le había hecho! The clues: a question or an exclamation in the third person, in the narrator's tense, without a speech verb and without a dash or quotation marks. Do not confuse it with a film's voice-over: a voz en off speaks in the first person, like direct style, and usually says what the character thinks as it happens.

explicacion.en: English writes dialogue with quotation marks and a comma. Spanish narrative opens each turn with a raya and introduces the narrator's comment with a second raya.
English puts a comma or a period before the verb. In Spanish there is no period before the narrator's comment, and the comment starts in lowercase because it is part of the same sentence.
After the comment you close with a second raya, and then you need punctuation: a comma if the sentence goes on, a period if a new sentence begins.

titulo.en: The dash opens every turn

texto.en: In Spanish narrative, a dialogue is written with the raya, a long dash (—), and not with quotation marks. The raya opens each speaker's turn, and each turn goes on a new line: —¿Dónde estás? —preguntó Emma. Notice that a question keeps its ¿…? and an exclamation keeps its ¡…!, and that the comment of the narrator, called el inciso narrativo, is introduced by a second raya. In this line it is preguntó Emma, with no period before it. English puts the words in quotation marks and the verb after a comma: “Where are you?” asked Emma. In Spanish you do not use both.

titulo.en: The comment of the narrator

texto.en: The comment starts in lowercase, even after a question or an exclamation, because it belongs to the same sentence: —¡No lo puedo creer! —exclamó Mateo. If the speech goes on after the comment, you close the comment with another raya. If the sentence continues, put a comma after that raya: —Ven —dijo Pedro—, te necesito. If a new sentence begins, put a period: —Ven —dijo Pedro—. Te necesito. The verb of the comment says how the voice sounds: decir, preguntar, susurrar (very quietly), exclamar (with emotion), murmurar (in a low voice), replicar and contestar (to answer). Do not confuse the raya with a hyphen (-), which is shorter and joins words. In careful writing you always use the raya; in the typing exercises of this lesson a hyphen is also accepted, only because the raya is hard to find on many keyboards.

traduccion.en: Yes. The narrator's comment has no period before it and starts with a lowercase letter, because it is part of the same sentence: “Come here,” she whispered.

dialogo.texto: ¿Y si la intervención sigue después del comentario? Por ejemplo, cuando ella dice por qué escondió la carta.

traduccion.en: And what if the speech continues after the comment? For example, when she says why she hid the letter.

traduccion.en: Then you close the comment with another dash. If the sentence goes on, you put a comma: “Come,” said Pedro, “I need you.” If another sentence begins, you put a period: “Come,” said Pedro. “I need you.”

dialogo.texto: Entiendo. Y los verbos de habla, ¿cuáles podemos usar? Yo siempre escribo «dijo», y suena repetido.

dialogo.texto: Hay muchos: preguntar, susurrar, exclamar, murmurar, replicar y contestar. Cada uno dice cómo suena la voz. «Susurró» es en voz baja; «exclamó» es con emoción; «replicó» es contestar cuando no estás de acuerdo.

traduccion.en: There are many: preguntar, susurrar, exclamar, murmurar, replicar and contestar. Each one tells how the voice sounds. “Susurró” is in a low voice; “exclamó” is with emotion; “replicó” is answering when you do not agree.

traduccion.en: Perfect. Notice the end: after the comment there is a dash, and then a period, because another sentence begins. And each speaker goes on a new line.

explicacion.en: English says “both of the brothers,” so learners add de. In Spanish ambos goes directly before the noun, with no article and no de. You can also say los dos hermanos.
Learners look for a singular form, as with “each.” Sendos has no singular: it already means one for each of several people, so it is always plural.
English both has no gender, so learners forget to match it. Ambos / ambas agree with the noun: ambas actrices, ambos actores.

titulo.en: Ambos: the two together

texto.en: Ambos (masculine) and ambas (feminine) mean los dos and las dos. They go before the noun, with no article, and they agree with it: ambos protagonistas, ambas actrices. Ambos is more common in writing and in formal speech: in daily conversation people say los dos. You can also use it alone, as a pronoun: Ambos buscan trabajo. English “both of the brothers” becomes ambos hermanos: Spanish does not say ambos de.

titulo.en: Sendos: one for each one

texto.en: Sendos (masculine) and sendas (feminine) mean one for each of the people or things already mentioned: Los hermanos recibieron sendas cartas means each brother received one letter (two letters in all). They exist only in the plural, they agree with the noun and they go before it: sendos premios, sendas maletas. Do not confuse them: ambos puts the two together, as in Ambos hermanos viajan, while sendos shares out one item to each, as in Llevan sendas maletas. They are formal words, typical of written comments about films, books and news. Sendos cannot be used when only one person receives something.

contexto.en: Friday, June 18, 2032, outside a movie theater. Emma, Mateo and Sofía Herrera have just seen a film about two brothers who travel to the capital to look for work. All three use tú with each other. They discuss the characters and the cast of the film.

dialogo.texto: ¡Qué película! ¿Qué les pareció, chicos?

traduccion.en: What a film! What did you think, guys?

dialogo.texto: Me encantó. Los dos protagonistas son muy distintos: uno es tímido y el otro es hablador. Pero ambos buscan trabajo en la capital, y ambos llegan sin dinero.

traduccion.en: I loved it. The two protagonists are very different: one is shy and the other is talkative. But both look for work in the capital, and both arrive without money.

dialogo.texto: Fíjate en las maletas. Los dos llevan sendas maletas, una vieja y una nueva, y cada maleta cuenta algo del carácter de su dueño.

traduccion.en: Notice the suitcases. They each carry a suitcase, one old and one new, and each suitcase tells something about the character of its owner.

dialogo.texto: Y no olvides el reparto. Es un reparto coral, con muchos personajes, y el guionista le da a cada uno su momento. Las dos actrices secundarias ganaron sendos premios en un festival.

traduccion.en: And do not forget the cast. It is an ensemble cast, with many characters, and the screenwriter gives each one a moment. The two supporting actresses won an award each at a festival.

dialogo.texto: Es el primer largometraje del director, ¿verdad? Y no es una adaptación de un libro: la historia es original.

traduccion.en: It is the director's first feature film, right? And it is not an adaptation of a book: the story is original.

dialogo.texto: Sí, y el estreno mundial fue en ese festival. Tanto el guionista como el director recibieron un galardón por esta película. Ambos recibieron sendos premios, y los dos subieron al escenario con su estatuilla.

traduccion.en: Yes, and the world premiere was at that festival. Both the screenwriter and the director received an award for this film. Both received an award each, and the two went up on the stage with their statuette.

dialogo.texto: ¿Y el final? Ambos hermanos consiguen trabajo, y los dos reciben sendas cartas de su madre.

traduccion.en: And the ending? Both brothers get a job, and the two receive a letter each from their mother.

dialogo.texto: Sí, las dos cartas dicen casi lo mismo, pero cada hermano la lee de otra forma.

traduccion.en: Yes, the two letters say almost the same thing, but each brother reads his own in another way.

dialogo.texto: Ahora entiendo la diferencia entre las dos palabras: «ambos» junta a los dos, y «sendos» reparte uno a cada uno.

traduccion.en: Now I understand the difference between the two words: “ambos” puts the two together, and “sendos” shares out one to each.

dialogo.texto: Exacto. «Ambos hermanos viajan» es lo que hacen juntos. «Llevan sendas maletas» es lo que lleva cada uno.

traduccion.en: Exactly. “Both brothers travel” is what they do together. “They carry a suitcase each” is what each one carries.

dialogo.texto: Y las dos palabras cambian con el género: ambos actores, ambas actrices, sendos premios, sendas cartas.

traduccion.en: And both words change with the gender: ambos actores, ambas actrices, sendos premios, sendas cartas.

dialogo.texto: Otra cosa: en una conversación decimos «los dos» más que «ambos», pero en un comentario escrito «ambos» suena mejor.

traduccion.en: Another thing: in a conversation we say “los dos” more than “ambos,” but in a written review “ambos” sounds better.

dialogo.texto: Muy bien, chicos. Entonces escribo en mi cuaderno: «ambos» es para los dos juntos, y «sendos» es para uno a cada uno.

traduccion.en: Very good, guys. So I write in my notebook: “ambos” is for the two together, and “sendos” is for one to each.

dialogo.texto: Voy a escribir un comentario sobre la película para el club. Primero hablo del reparto, y después de los dos hermanos.

traduccion.en: I am going to write a review of the film for the club. First I talk about the cast, and then about the two brothers.

dialogo.texto: Buena idea. Puedes empezar así: «En este largometraje, ambos hermanos buscan trabajo y llevan sendas maletas.»

traduccion.en: Good idea. You can start like this: “In this feature film, both brothers look for work and carry a suitcase each.”

dialogo.texto: Y puedes terminar con el estreno mundial y los premios. Yo te ayudo, si quieres.

traduccion.en: And you can end with the world premiere and the awards. I will help you, if you want.

dialogo.texto: Perfecto. Gracias, chicos. Esta noche escribo el comentario, y mañana se lo cuento a los dos.

traduccion.en: Perfect. Thanks, guys. Tonight I write the review, and tomorrow I tell you both about it.

dialogo.texto: Muy bien, Mateo. Nos vemos el jueves 24 en el club, con las dos palabras bien aprendidas.

traduccion.en: Very good, Mateo. See you on Thursday the 24th at the club, with both words well learned.

objetivo.en: Recommend a work with arguments using no hay nadie / ninguna… que + subjunctive.

traduccion.en: the praise, the compliment

nota.en: Say “eh-LOH-hyoh”: the g before i sounds like a strong h. An elogio is a positive comment about a person or a work.

nota.en: Say “HWEE-syoh deh bah-LOHR”: the j sounds like a strong h and the c like an s. “La mejor novela” is a juicio de valor: it needs arguments.

traduccion.en: the rereading

nota.en: Say “rreh-lehk-TOO-rah”: the first r is rolled. The prefix re- means again: releer, to read again.

traduccion.en: the side comment, the short note added to a text

nota.en: Say “ah-pohs-TEE-yah”: the ll sounds like the y in “yes”. An apostilla is a brief comment added to clarify or complete what was said.

traduccion.en: recommendable, worth recommending

nota.en: Say “rreh-koh-mehn-DAH-bleh”: the first r is rolled. It is an adjective: una novela recomendable, un libro recomendable.

traduccion.en: to move, to excite emotionally

nota.en: Say “eh-moh-syoh-NAHR”: the c sounds like an s. La película me emocionó = the film moved me.

traduccion.en: to recommend

nota.en: Say “rreh-koh-mehn-DAHR”: the first r is rolled. It is a stem-changing verb: recomiendo, recomiendas, recomienda.

traduccion.en: the reader

nota.en: Say “lehk-TOHR”: the stress is on the last syllable. For a woman: la lectora.

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: No hay nadie que conoce el final.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: No hay nadie que conozca el final.

explicacion.en: English “there is nobody who knows” uses a plain present, so learners keep the indicative. In Spanish, a person who does not exist needs the subjunctive: conozca.

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: No hay ninguna novela que me ha emocionado tanto.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: No hay ninguna novela que me haya emocionado tanto.

explicacion.en: The tense is right (present perfect), but the mood is not: after no hay ninguna … que, haber must be in the subjunctive, haya, not ha.

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: Hay alguien que conozca el final: Mateo.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: Hay alguien que conoce el final: Mateo.

explicacion.en: Once you have learned the subjunctive it is tempting to use it after every hay … que. But when you know the person exists (here, Mateo), Spanish uses the indicative: conoce. The subjunctive is for a negated or unknown person: No hay nadie que conozca… / ¿Hay alguien que conozca…?

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: No hay nadie que no la recomienda.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: No hay nadie que no la recomiende.

explicacion.en: The double negative does not change the rule: the clause after nadie que still needs the subjunctive, recomiende, even though the meaning is positive (everybody recommends it).

titulo.en: Does it exist or not?

texto.en: After a noun, the verb of the clause with que depends on whether the person or thing exists. If it exists, use the indicative: Hay una novela que me encanta. Hay alguien que conoce el final. If you say that it does not exist, use the subjunctive: No hay nadie que conozca el final. No hay ninguna novela que me encante. If you ask whether it exists, use the subjunctive too: ¿Hay alguna novela que te haya emocionado más? Think of it this way: you cannot point to the person or the thing, so the verb is subjunctive. Ninguno and ninguna are used in the singular: ninguna novela, ningún libro.

titulo.en: Recommending with arguments

texto.en: For experiences up to now you will often need the present perfect subjunctive, haya + participle: No hay ninguna película que me haya emocionado tanto. A double negative is a strong form of praise: No hay nadie que no recomiende esta película means that everyone recommends it. When you recommend a work, remember that “it is the best” is a juicio de valor: add two arguments with porque and además.

contexto.en: Thursday, June 24, 2032, in the café in La Floresta. It is the last session of the reading club. Sofía, Mateo and Emma use tú with each other. They choose which work to recommend to the students of the institute and, at the end, Sofía suggests preparing the DELE C1 together next year.

dialogo.texto: Esta es nuestra última sesión del club, y tenemos una tarea importante: elegir qué obra recomendar a los alumnos del instituto. ¿Quién empieza?

traduccion.en: This is our last session of the club, and we have an important task: choosing which work to recommend to the students at the institute. Who starts?

dialogo.texto: Yo propongo «Cien años de soledad». No hay ninguna novela que me haya hecho reír y llorar a la vez como esa. Además, no hay nadie que no la recomiende.

traduccion.en: I propose “Cien años de soledad.” There is no novel that has made me laugh and cry at the same time like that one. Besides, there is nobody who does not recommend it.

dialogo.texto: Es una gran novela, pero decir que es «la mejor» es un juicio de valor, y los alumnos necesitan argumentos. Además, no hay nadie que la pueda leer de una sola vez. Tiene muchos personajes con el mismo nombre, y los lectores se pierden.

traduccion.en: It is a great novel, but saying that it is “the best” is a value judgment, and the students need arguments. Besides, there is nobody who can read it in one sitting. It has many characters with the same name, and readers get lost.

dialogo.texto: Es verdad, pero esa dificultad forma parte de la novela. Y hay un elogio que se repite en todas partes: la relectura siempre descubre algo nuevo.

traduccion.en: That is true, but that difficulty is part of the novel. And there is a compliment that is repeated everywhere: rereading always discovers something new.

dialogo.texto: Yo tengo una idea. ¿Hay alguna manera de ayudar a los lectores nuevos? Yo recomiendo empezar con el primer capítulo y usar un árbol genealógico. Así no hay nadie que se pierda entre tantos personajes.

traduccion.en: I have an idea. Is there any way to help new readers? I recommend starting with the first chapter and using a family tree. That way there is nobody who gets lost among so many characters.

dialogo.texto: Me gusta. Una apostilla: el árbol genealógico es una ayuda, no una obligación. Cada lector decide cómo leer.

traduccion.en: I like it. A side note: the family tree is an aid, not an obligation. Each reader decides how to read.

dialogo.texto: Entonces, ¿qué escribimos en la recomendación? Necesitamos dos argumentos.

traduccion.en: So, what do we write in the recommendation? We need two arguments.

dialogo.texto: Primero, es recomendable porque tiene mucho humor. Segundo, no hay ninguna historia que mezcle tan bien lo real con lo imposible.

traduccion.en: First, it is recommendable because it has a lot of humor. Second, there is no story that mixes the real and the impossible so well.

dialogo.texto: Muy bien. Y ahora una pregunta para los dos: ¿hay alguna novela que los haya emocionado más que esta?

traduccion.en: Very good. And now a question for both of you: is there any novel that has moved you more than this one?

dialogo.texto: Para mí, hay una que me encanta: «Pedro Páramo». Pero no hay ninguna novela que me haya hecho llorar tanto como esa.

traduccion.en: For me, there is one that I love: “Pedro Páramo.” But there is no novel that has made me cry as much as that one.

dialogo.texto: Y para mí no hay ninguna que me haya emocionado más que «Cien años de soledad». ¡Ya lo dije!

traduccion.en: And for me there is none that has moved me more than “Cien años de soledad.” I already said it!

dialogo.texto: Perfecto. Entonces recomendamos las dos obras: una para empezar y otra para releer. Y una última cosa: el año que viene, ¿preparamos juntos el DELE C1?

traduccion.en: Perfect. Then we recommend both works: one to start with and another to reread. And one last thing: next year, shall we prepare the DELE C1 together?

dialogo.texto: ¡Claro! Yo quiero participar. Será un buen proyecto para los tres.

traduccion.en: Of course! I want to take part. It will be a good project for the three of us.

dialogo.texto: Yo también. Y para empezar el año con ganas, voy a leer «Cien años de soledad» otra vez.

traduccion.en: Me too. And to start the year with enthusiasm, I am going to read “Cien años de soledad” again.

dialogo.texto: Gracias por este mes de lecturas, chicos. Fue muy bonito, y ustedes dos son excelentes lectores.

traduccion.en: Thank you for this month of readings, guys. It was very nice, and you two are excellent readers.

dialogo.texto: Gracias a ti, Sofía. Aprendí mucho, y ahora leo con otros ojos, y también escribo mejor.

traduccion.en: Thank you, Sofía. I learned a lot, and now I read with different eyes, and I also write better.
